text:
Kate: quick heads-up — I'm proposing we split the 'metrics_payload' JSONB into a small set of typed columns (route_id, tenant_id, quota_window, token_estimate, status_flags) and keep a trimmed jsonb blob for the rest. Goal: speed up console queries, reduce p99 dashboards, and enable indexable quota filters.

Sam: curious about dual-write complexity. Are we doing a shadow write + backfill, or a phased write-schema approach?

Kate: phased. Plan: 1) add new nullable columns + triggers to populate from existing jsonb on write (dual-write for the app layer), 2) run a background backfill to populate historical rows, 3) flip read index in console service to prefer columns, 4) drop jsonb fields after metrics stable.

Anil: how big is the backfill window? We have ~14TB of telemetry events. Need an estimate on time & IO.

Kate: rough calc from sampling: ~120M rows, avg row payload 1.2KB. Backfill CPU-bound extraction + sequential scan -> estimated 48–72 hours if we parallelize per-partition (8 workers per shard). I/O ~160GB of read + writes to new columns. We'll throttle to avoid saturating replicas.

Morgan: what about reads during cutover? Console queries must remain correct. We should do a read-gate that does: prefer columns, fallback to jsonb if columns null. Add a feature flag to control.

Kate: exactly. Pseudocode for read preference:```sql
SELECT COALESCE(route_id_col, (metrics_payload->>'route')::uuid) AS route_id
FROM telemetry_events
WHERE ts >= $1 AND (route_id_col IS NOT NULL OR metrics_payload ? 'route');
```

Sam: any indexing plan? If we add route_id and quota_window indexes, these will balloon. We should consider partial indexes (e.g., where route_id_col IS NOT NULL) and also a synthetic composite index for common console filters.

Kate: agreed. Proposed indexes: partial btree on (route_id_col) WHERE route_id_col IS NOT NULL; gin trigram left on the trimmed jsonb for ad-hoc search; composite on (route_id_col, ts DESC) for recent-route charts. We'll monitor bloat.

Anil: constraints/compat — mobile and batch ingesters still write full jsonb. Triggers might break on old clients. Do we plan a migration window where we accept legacy writes?

Kate: triggers only populate columns if payload contains keys; app will be updated to write both (jsonb + columns) behind feature flag. We'll keep trigger logic lightweight: only set columns when present. We'll document client contract: new keys optional for a month, then required.

db-migrate-bot: migration job queued: analytics.column_split.phase1_v1 (DDL add columns) scheduled 2026-04-01 03:00 UTC, estimated 2h.

Morgan: rollout UX — add a Console banner explaining 'temporary query migration' and link to rollback page. Also we need a dashboard tracking how many rows have columns populated + query latencies by route.

Kate: added telemetry goals: target 2x median query speed on dashboard widgets, p99 down 30%. I'll add custom evals and alerts for when fallback-to-jsonb rate > 5% over 10m.

Sam: one more: backfill safety — include idempotency key and checkpointing by partition range. We'll need a resumable job.

Kate: yes job will checkpoint per-day partition and emit metrics per-range. I'll post the runbook after DDL lands.

Anil: sounds good. If we can get an A/B canary on a small tenant set first that'd give confidence.

Kate: canary on 5 big tenants planned for phase2. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Morgan: ping @oncall before DDL, and let's schedule a short post-mortem sync after first backfill.

Kate: will do.
